originalTitle: Thousands of Canadians call for US ambassador's expulsion
summary: An online petition accusing Pete Hoekstra of diplomatic interference in Canadian domestic affairs has garnered more than 60,000 signatures.
content:
More than 70,000 Canadians have signed a petition calling for the US ambassador in Ottawa to be expelled for undermining diplomatic relations between the two neighbours.

The online petition accuses Pete Hoekstra of "making repeated interventions in Canadian political discourse" and of having "normalised the Trump administration's threats to annex Canada as the '51st state'" of the US.

In a statement to the BBC, the US embassy said it was aware of the petition but declined to comment further.

Canada and the US are currently engaged in intense period of trade talks, aiming to reach an agreement before new US tariffs take effect next Wednesday.

The petition, launched by a woman in Calgary, also raises concerns about meetings in Washington between the US state department officials and some Albertans who want the province to separate from Canada.

It requests Ambassador Hoekstra be formally removed from his role, and a parliamentary committee review "US diplomatic interference in Canadian domestic affairs".

Leanne Walker, who initiated the petition, said the response had been a surprise.

"It's beyond what I expected out of this," she told state broadcaster CBC News , external .

"It tells me that it's not a fringe issue, and that a lot of Canadians are uncomfortable with how Hoekstra has been repeating Trump talking points about our sovereignty and Canada as a whole."

A Republican and a Trump ally, Hoekstra has been a fierce defender of US President Donald Trump's trade policies, saying they are meant to secure the safety and prosperity of Americans.

He has also described the relationship between the two countries critical.

But his time in Canada has not been low key.

There was a dust-up between Hoekstra and Ontario's trade representative , and the ambassador has been criticised for reposting Trump's comments about Canada becoming the 51st state and telling reporters it would be a "great discussion to be had" , external by the leaders of the two countries.

Most recently, he faced criticism for inviting one of the leaders of the 2022 Freedom Convoy movement to his official Fourth of July celebration.

He has also described some of the political rhetoric in Canada as "anti-American" and has frequently expressed frustration at the decision by most provinces to remove US alcohol from store shelves - a key point of friction in the current trade talks.

The petition for his recall will be tabled in parliament later this year by Green Party leader Elizabeth May.

In a statement to the BBC, May's office said that "she has an obligation to sponsor petitions brought forward by citizens, regardless of whether she personally agrees with what the petition is asking for".

The House of Commons allows for Canadians to submit petitions, and there are dozens open at any given time, many receiving just a few hundred signatures.

Once a petition, which must be submitted by a Canadian resident, is authorised by member of parliament, it is posted on parliament's website. If it reaches at least 500 valid signatures, it is then presented in the House and requires a government response.

The petition reached that bar as of Wednesday morning, garnering more than enough support to be presented in Canada's House of Commons.

It comes at a time when Canadian negotiators are working urgently to avert a planned 50% American tariff on roughly $20bn to $28bn in Canadian goods.

Last month, Trump announced the proposed tariffs in retaliation for what he called "unequal treatment" of US cars, dairy and alcohol.

Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney warned in response that a potential further retaliation was on the table if the new tariffs were enforced.

Canadian media have reported that an interim deal could be reached by Ottawa and Washington in the coming days.

chineseTitle: 数千加拿大人呼吁驱逐美国大使
chineseSummary: 一份指责皮特·霍克斯特拉（Pete Hoekstra）外交干涉加拿大内政的在线请愿书已获得超过 60,000 个签名。
chineseContent:
超过7万加拿大人签署了一份请愿书，要求驱逐美国驻渥太华大使，理由是他破坏了两个邻国之间的外交关系。

在线请愿书指责皮特·霍克斯特拉“反复干预加拿大政治话语”，并“将特朗普政府吞并加拿大作为美国‘第51个州’的威胁正常化”。

美国大使馆在给英国广播公司的一份声明中表示，它已了解请愿书，但拒绝进一步置评。

加拿大和美国目前正在进行紧张的贸易谈判，目标是在美国新关税下周三生效之前达成协议。

该请愿书由卡尔加里的一名妇女发起，还引起了人们对美国国务院官员和一些希望该省从加拿大分离的阿尔伯塔人在华盛顿举行的会议的担忧。

它要求正式解除霍克斯特拉大使的职务，并要求议会委员会审查“美国对加拿大内政的外交干涉”。

请愿书的发起人莉安·沃克表示，得到的回应令人惊讶。

“这超出了我的预期，”她告诉国家广播公司 CBC News（外部）。

“这告诉我，这不是一个边缘问题，而且许多加拿大人对霍克斯特拉重复特朗普关于我们主权和整个加拿大的观点感到不安。”

作为共和党人和特朗普的盟友，霍克斯特拉一直是美国总统唐纳德·特朗普贸易政策的坚定捍卫者，称这些政策旨在确保美国人的安全和繁荣。

他还形容两国关系至关重要。

但他在加拿大的日子并不低调。

霍克斯特拉和安大略省贸易代表之间发生了争执，这位大使因转发特朗普关于加拿大成为第51个州的评论并告诉记者这将是两国领导人在外部进行的“一场伟大的讨论”而受到批评。

最近，他因邀请 2022 年自由车队运动的一位领导人参加他的官方国庆节庆祝活动而受到批评。

他还将加拿大的一些政治言论描述为“反美”，并经常对大多数省份将美国酒类从商店货架上撤下的决定表示失望——这是当前贸易谈判中的一个关键摩擦点。

绿党领袖伊丽莎白·梅将于今年晚些时候向议会提交罢免他的请愿书。

在给英国广播公司的一份声明中，梅的办公室表示，“她有义务赞助公民提出的请愿书，无论她个人是否同意请愿书的要求”。

下议院允许加拿大人提交请愿书，并且在任何特定时间都会有数十份请愿书开放，其中许多只收到了几百个签名。

请愿书必须由加拿大居民提交，一旦获得议会成员的授权，就会发布在议会的网站上。如果达到至少 500 个有效签名，则会在众议院提交并要求政府做出回应。

请愿书于周三上午到达该酒吧，获得了足够多的支持，可以在加拿大下议院提交。

与此同时，加拿大谈判代表正在紧急努力避免美国计划对价值约 200 亿至 280 亿美元的加拿大商品征收 50% 的关税。

上个月，特朗普宣布了拟议的关税，以报复他所谓的美国汽车、乳制品和酒类的“不平等待遇”。

加拿大总理马克·卡尼回应称，如果新关税得到执行，可能会出现进一步报复。

加拿大媒体报道称，渥太华和华盛顿可能在未来几天内达成一项临时协议。
